quantities.V1: connected design load of the installation or system under review (kVA)
quantities.V2: measured voltage-drop / harmonic distortion ratio at the point of common coupling
quantities.V3: required spare capacity or fault-current margin reserve (kVA)
quantities.V4: rated capacity of the supplying transformer or feeder (kVA)
quantities.ANNEX_SEVERITY: severity of the deficiency recorded in the inspection or complaint-investigation annex

tier3_rule: demand_load * (1 - REG.failure_derate_rate * eff_sev) - REG.retrofit_margin * REG.thermal_stress_mult * V3
draft.rationale: An electrical engineer's case file sizes an installation: connected load (V1) is reduced to a diversified demand load using the supplying transformer or feeder rating (V4), and a spare-capacity or fault-margin reserve (V3) is added. The treatment is the approved design capacity. The three public rules follow the core tasks. A conforming installation is signed off with a small reserve. A code-style voltage-drop derating scales with the measured drop ratio (V2). An explicit inspection deficiency cuts capacity by the annex severity. The unwritten convention is the practice of harmonic derating: practitioners apply a steeper severity derating once distortion passes about 15%, a threshold that is not a published code cutoff, and give back some feeder headroom. The precedent rule covers failure and complaint investigations. In those cases, thermal stress amplifies severity in proportion to distortion. Prior root-cause findings also fix the derating rate and the retrofit margin taken from reserve.
